query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: infrastructure_domain
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated categories (email, database, VPN, network) derived from ticket content. Resolution time can be meaningfully compared across these domains, complementing the given 'category' column with a technical-domain lens.

per_column.name: problem_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity levels (outage_system_wide, partial_access, performance_degraded) form an ordered, interpretable scale that plausibly associates with resolution_time and supports segmentation.

per_column.name: resolution_completion_status
per_column.rationale: A boolean of whether the ticket was resolved/closed. This is downstream of and near-tautological with resolution_time (unresolved tickets have no/ongoing resolution time); it restates the focus rather than offering an external associational variable.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope categories (system_wide, single_user, department_scoped) are interpretable and well-separated, and blast radius plausibly relates to how long resolution takes. Note partial overlap with problem_severity, but still a distinct segmentation axis.

per_column.name: authentication_access_failure
per_column.rationale: A clear binary flag with reasonable class balance (76/424) marking auth/access issues; a plausible, interpretable dimension to compare resolution times against.

per_column.name: technician_assignment_continuity
per_column.rationale: Whether the ticket stayed with one technician vs. was reassigned; balanced binary (216/284) and process-oriented, directly plausible as a driver of resolution time and interpretable for a human explorer.

judge.rationale: Five of six columns are external, interpretable, well-separated segmentations (domain, severity, scope, auth flag, assignment continuity) that a human can group on and compare against resolution_time, going beyond the given category/priority/group. Several overlap conceptually (severity vs. scope vs. auth), slightly reducing distinctiveness. The main failure is resolution_completion_status, which is essentially a restatement of the focus (resolution outcome) and offers no independent relationship. Overall a strong EDA-oriented set with one tautological inclusion.
